cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is passing along a message from the LORD, and this one is addressed to Babylon, the great empire of the Chaldeans. The LORD speaks to her like royalty: 'O Virgin Daughter of Babylon.' But friend, He is NOT here to fluff her pillows.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Daughter of Babylon to go down and sit in the ___, with no throne.
The LORD says Babylon will keep being called tender and delicate.

cards.text: Then the princess gets a job change, and it is NOT a promotion. The LORD tells her to take millstones, and friend, I know that move: I went from the kitchen counter to the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell the Daughter of Babylon to do with the millstones?

cards.text: She's told to remove her veil and wade through the streams. The LORD says her shame will be exposed.

cards.question: The LORD tells Babylon He will take vengeance and spare no one.

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of the message, a line breaks in to tell us whose words these are. It calls Him 'Our Redeemer.'

cards.question: In the middle of the message to Babylon, the passage names who 'Our Redeemer' is. Who is it?

cards.text: Back to the LORD's words for Babylon: 'Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of the Chaldeans.' Friend, that's not a time-out, that's somebody closing the drawer on you.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Daughter of the Chaldeans she'll lose a title. What will she no longer be called?

cards.text: Then the LORD explains how His own people ended up in Babylon's hands. He was angry with His people, and He placed them under Babylon's control.

cards.question: Once God's people were under Babylon's control, how did Babylon treat them?
Babylon went easy on the elderly among God's people.

cards.text: And Babylon? Babylon's talking like that crown is GLUED on.

cards.question: Babylon said, 'I will be ___ forever.'
Babylon thought carefully about where all of this would lead.

cards.text: Now the LORD gives Babylon a new nickname: 'O lover of luxury who sits securely.' And then He tells us exactly what she says to herself.

cards.question: What does Babylon, the lover of luxury who sits securely, say to herself?

answers.text: I need someone to help me

cards.text: She's so sure of herself, friend, she names two kinds of grief that will never touch her.

cards.question: Babylon says she will never be a ___ or know the loss of ___.

cards.text: The LORD says those two things will overtake her in a moment, in a single day. That's not a slow bake, friend, that's the timer going off before you've even shut the oven door.

cards.question: Babylon's many sorceries and powerful spells will keep those losses away.

cards.text: Babylon felt secure in her wickedness and said, 'No one sees me.' That's me hiding a cookie behind my back with crumbs ALL over my mustache.

cards.question: The LORD says Babylon's ___ and knowledge led her astray.

cards.text: But disaster is coming, and Babylon won't know how to charm it away or ward it off.

cards.question: How does the LORD say the devastation will happen to Babylon?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Babylon to take her stand with her spells and sorceries, the ones she's worn herself out with since her youth. And He adds, 'Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror!'

cards.question: The LORD already said Babylon can't ward off this calamity. So when He says 'Perhaps you will succeed,' what is He doing?

cards.text: Next He calls on her counselors, the astrologers who observe the stars and monthly predict her fate. My boy Berry watched the stars every night too, but he NEVER sold anybody a monthly forecast.

cards.question: The LORD tells Babylon's counselors to come forward now and save her.

cards.text: Then the LORD shows what those astrologers really are.

cards.question: Babylon's astrologers are like ___ that the fire burns up.
When the fire comes for Babylon's astrologers, there will be coals left over to warm them.

cards.text: Last, the LORD turns to the people Babylon has labored and traded with since her youth.

cards.question: What does the LORD say each of Babylon's trading partners does?

cards.text: Spells, star-watchers, trading partners. Everybody Babylon leaned on, and not one of them can save her.

findings.problem: The card says verse 4 'breaks in to tell us whose words these are.' Isaiah 47:4 only says, 'Our Redeemer—the LORD of Hosts is His name—is the Holy One of Israel.' It never says it is naming the speaker of the message, so the card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the message is 'from the LORD,' and cards 1 through 7 all say 'The LORD' is the one speaking. Card 8 then says verse 4 tells 'whose words these are.' Together these give away 'The LORD of Hosts' and rule out Cyrus and Isaiah before the baker picks.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke 'that's not a time-out' uses a time-out, which is a way of disciplining children. That is a scenario aimed at kids.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids.

findings.problem: Story card 5 already says the losses will come 'in a moment, in a single day' and compares it to a timer going off before the oven door is shut. That rules out the wrong answers 'Slowly over many years' and 'After a long siege' before card 10 asks how the devastation will happen.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Story card 13 says 'He calls on her counselors.' That gives away the answer to the true-or-false on card 14, which asks whether the LORD tells the counselors to come forward.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The statement marked True says the LORD tells the counselors to come forward. In Isaiah 47:13 He is speaking to Babylon about them: 'let them come forward now and save you.' The card changes who is being spoken to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD 'turns to' a new group, the people Babylon traded with. Card 19 calls them 'trading partners,' and card 20 lists them separately from the star-watchers. Isaiah 47:15 ('This is what they are to you—those with whom you have labored and traded from youth') leaves open whether these are the same astrologers and sorcerers from verses 12 to 14. The text also never says the LORD speaks to them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Spells, star-watchers, trading partners. Everybody Babylon leaned on,' which repeats earlier cards instead of moving the passage forward. It also extends verse 15's 'not one of them can save you' to all three groups.
